summary: Dual-webhook lead capture + secured GET /api/leads tested end-to-end. Backend pytest suite (7 tests) all pass. Frontend UI flow verified: Step1 validation blocks advance; Step2->Step3 triggers POST /api/leads/partial creating a record with lead_stage='form_submitted' and empty preferred_date/time; Step3 empty submit validation blocks submit; Step3 full submit shows apply-success panel and record is UPSERTED to lead_stage='appointment_requested' with preferred_date + preferred_time (exactly 1 record per email — no duplicates). Admin GET /api/leads returns 403 without header, 200 with correct key. Landing page hero renders with no console errors.
critical_code_review_comments: Optional: goStep3() in AppointmentForm.jsx fires axios.post to /leads/partial with .catch(()=>{}) — silent failure is fine for drop-off capture but no observability. Consider logging via a lightweight beacon or Sentry breadcrumb.
Optional: _forward_to_webhook uses blocking `requests` inside asyncio.to_thread — acceptable, but httpx.AsyncClient would fit better in an async FastAPI app.
Minor: ADMIN_API_KEY check should also reject empty x_admin_key even before comparing (already handled — ok).
seed_data_creation: Test leads with emails prefixed TEST_ and qa+ were created in the leads collection during backend + UI tests.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Dual webhook split verified. Partial (form_submitted) fires on step-2 -> step-3 transition (fire-and-forget). Full (appointment_requested) fires on step-3 submit. Upsert-by-email works: only 1 record per email regardless of partial+full sequence. Admin key auth on GET /api/leads works. Do not run pytest concurrently with itself against the same DB — no locking issues seen but tests use unique timestamped emails so re-runs are safe.
